source.title: Measuring Progress in Dictionary Learning for Language Model Interpretability with Board Game Models
source.authors: Adam Karvonen; Benjamin Wright; C. Rager; Rico Angell; Jannik Brinkmann; L. Smith; C. M. Verdun; David Bau; Samuel Marks

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Evaluates SAE-recoverable features in chess- and Othello-trained language models, a board-game setting rather than the toy superposition setup or ordinary language-model settings named in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper measures SAE coverage and board reconstruction for specified board-state properties. It does not test superposition geometry, feature sparsity or importance transitions, capacity competition, or polysemanticity. Statements about superposition and prior studies are background citations, not results here. Training hyperparameters and metric definitions are not results rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on two small transformer LMs (chess, Othello) and scores how well dictionary features recover researcher-specified board-state properties, against random-weight and linear-probe references. This bears on V4 (SAE-recoverable sparse features in LMs, here board-game LMs rather than ordinary LLMs) and on V5's completeness part. It does not test toy geometry, capacity, polysemanticity causes or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also stress that SAEs on random-weight models perform very poorly, so SAE recovery reflects the trained models' learned structure. They propose coverage and reconstruction as metrics of monosemanticity and exhaustiveness, and p-annealing as an improvement.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates SAE dictionaries and their recovery of board-game properties; it does not reproduce the original toy superposition experiments or their geometry measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery scores vary substantially by board-state property and by domain. The paper also reports differences by SAE architecture, training method, hidden dimension, and metric.
record.problems: The tested language models are restricted to chess and Othello. The candidate property sets are researcher-specified and may omit relevant features. SAE recovery is weaker than linear-probe performance, and the results do not establish that SAE features are stable or canonical.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5 reports per-property reconstruction and coverage scores for SAEs on a randomly initialized chess-architecture model. Those 30 rows were omitted because the 60-row limit would require dropping reported main-model property results; Table 1's random-model aggregate controls are retained in r5-r8. Table 4 linear-probe per-property values are also omitted; Table 1 retains aggregate linear-probe comparators.

untested.parts: No toy-model geometry, sparsity transition or near-orthogonality measurements.
No capacity competition or importance-based allocation.
No analysis of the causes of polysemanticity.
Spreading of features across neurons; ordinary natural-language LLMs.
Stability across seeds and canonicality are not tested directly; only completeness for researcher-chosen properties.
No test of 1-D vs multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Per-property random-weight SAE baselines (needed to judge r13-r42)
Per-property linear-probe F1 as ceiling for each SAE row
Coverage/reconstruction by SAE method and expansion factor (8192 beats 4096)
Layer-1 SAE control scoring 0.01 board reconstruction

record.verdict_notes: Chess board_state aggregates disagree between Table 1 (coverage 0.48, reconstruction 0.85) and Table 4 (0.41, 0.67). Several 'observed' chess properties (queen, bishop_pair, castling) are largely recoverable by SAEs on a random model, so they are weak evidence of learned features. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No test of overlapping or nearly orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular superposition geometry.
No test of capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or polysemantic neurons.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether polysemanticity evidences superposition.
Tests SAE recovery of board-game properties, not feature distribution across neurons or recovery in ordinary LLMs.
Tests SAE coverage and reconstruction for selected board properties, but not feature stability or canonicality; the property catalog is researcher-specified.
No comparison of one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

relationships.condition: Board-state piece reconstruction in chess and Othello LMs, and chess check, en passant and can_capture_queen
relationships.reason: SAE scores far exceed random-weight baselines: reconstruction 0.85 vs 0.01 and 0.95 vs 0.08, check 1.00 vs 0.00, en passant 0.92 vs 0.00 (r2, r4, r13, r14, r17, r33, r34).
relationships.display_finding: Against random-weight baselines, board reconstruction scored 0.85 vs 0.01 and 0.95 vs 0.08, check 1.00 vs 0.00 and en passant 0.92 vs 0.00.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Board-state piece reconstruction in chess and Othello LMs, and chess check, en passant and can_capture_queen
source_check.reason: Tables 1, 4 and 5 show substantial recovery above random-weight controls in these conditions.

relationships.condition: Coverage of single features per property, and complex chess strategy properties
relationships.reason: Coverage is only about half (0.48, 0.52), strategy properties score low, and several properties barely beat random-weight SAEs (r1, r3, r15, r16, r18-r32, r35-r42).
relationships.display_finding: Single-feature coverage was only about half (0.48 and 0.52), strategy properties scored low, and several properties barely beat SAEs trained on random-weight models.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Coverage of single features per property, and complex chess strategy properties
source_check.reason: Single-feature matching and strategy recovery are incomplete or only slightly above controls. Some strategy properties also have low probe scores, so their presence in the model is uncertain.

relationships.condition: Completeness of SAE features relative to linearly decodable board information (chess especially)
relationships.reason: Chess reconstruction is 0.85 vs probe 0.98, coverage is about 0.5, and the authors state SAEs do not capture all information (r1, r2, r3, r15, r29, r31, r39-r42).
relationships.display_finding: Chess reconstruction scored 0.85 vs 0.98 for a linear probe, coverage was about 0.5, and the authors state SAEs do not capture all the information.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: Completeness of SAE features relative to linearly decodable board information (chess especially)
source_check.reason: Recovery is substantial but incomplete: chess reconstruction is 0.85 against probe 0.98. Under the verdict rules, incomplete effects warrant limits_scope; stability and canonicity are untested.

relationships.condition: Dependence of recovered features on SAE training method and dictionary size
relationships.reason: From the text (Figs 2-4), not rows: coverage differs by method (p-annealing, gated) and is higher at 8192 than at 4096 latents.
relationships.display_finding: Coverage differed between methods such as p-annealing and gated SAEs, and was higher with 8192 latents than with 4096.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Dependence of recovered features on SAE training method and dictionary size
source_check.reason: Section 5 reports recovery improvements with p-annealing and larger dictionaries, qualifying completeness for the tested SAEs. These comparisons do not establish instability or noncanonical feature identities.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Board-state piece reconstruction in chess and Othello LMs, and chess check, en passant and can_capture_queen
labels.reason: Tables 1, 4 and 5 show substantial recovery above random-weight controls in these conditions.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Coverage of single features per property, and complex chess strategy properties
labels.reason: Single-feature matching and strategy recovery are incomplete or only slightly above controls. Some strategy properties also have low probe scores, so their presence in the model is uncertain.

labels.label: challenges
labels.condition: Completeness of SAE features relative to linearly decodable board information (chess especially)
labels.reason: Recovery is substantial but incomplete: chess reconstruction is 0.85 against probe 0.98. Under the verdict rules, incomplete effects warrant limits_scope; stability and canonicity are untested.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Dependence of recovered features on SAE training method and dictionary size
labels.reason: Section 5 reports recovery improvements with p-annealing and larger dictionaries, qualifying completeness for the tested SAEs. These comparisons do not establish instability or noncanonical feature identities.

relation.reason: The study measures recovery of specified board properties against random-weight controls and linear probes.

tranche.reason: Board-game language models provide a new setting with direct results on SAE recovery and completeness.

source_check.notes: Table 1 and Table 4 give unexplained differing chess aggregates: coverage 0.48 versus 0.41 and reconstruction 0.85 versus 0.67. Coverage is mean maximal F1, not a fraction of recovered concepts; completeness conclusions depend on the specified BSPs and recovery rule.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Chess and Othello board-game language models; board-state properties with relatively high SAE scores
reader_labels.reason: SAEs recover several specified properties with high scores, including Othello board reconstruction 0.95 and chess check, queen, and castling properties; see r4, r13-r14, r19-r28, r33-r34, and r37.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Chess strategy and board-state properties with lower SAE scores; board-game model setting
reader_labels.reason: Recovery varies by property and is incomplete for several measures, including fork, pin, can_check, and aggregate board_state; the paper also limits generalizability beyond chess and Othello. See r15-r18, r29-r32, r35-r36, and r39-r42.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Completeness of SAE recovery for the tested board-state properties
reader_labels.reason: SAE reconstruction falls below the linear-probe reference on both games in Table 1, and multiple property-specific scores are incomplete; this challenges completeness for the tested properties, not stability or canonicality. See r1-r4, r9-r12, and r15-r18, r29-r32, r35-r42.
